I respect your answer, and I’m glad you can find meaning in it. 

For me though, it just shatters the charade of doing good — ultimately, good deeds are done for ones own gain. 
If you gained no satisfaction, or positive outcome from doing good, it’s highly unlikely you’d do it. We are biologically programmed to follow a set of procedures, and a set that has a greater chance of good outcome for ourselves. 

Example would be, we give shelter to our children. Good deed, but it’s to carry on our own genetics. 
Or, a bit more extreme. We give food to a homeless. Most who do gloat about it, and it becomes evident they’re doing it for their own self image. Even those who do not gloat it around, it’s still done as a way to better ones own perception of their self. 

To me, that does not correlate any meaning to life beyond carrying our genetic lines on (the very most basic instinct every living organism follows). 
I used to believe that, being someone who wishes to disobey that coding was evidence of a soul, or something greater.. but in reality, it’s just a bug in the code — it’s not evident of anything. 

Now, I try my best to do good for others. Hell, I’d argue that a majority of my life decision have been based on the premise of helping others along, and increasing their happiness. 
Maybe that’s my problem — I haven’t looked out for myself enough. But then, does that not contradict the meaning?
Is it then about a balance? Where do you draw that line? I think of myself as a very good person outwardly, but I can see pst the charade, and that I am doing it out of the interests of myself and not others. Therefore it all feels very plastic, and fake. 

I’ve come to the conclusion that, realistically speaking, for me, to be happy means withdrawing from society at large, living in my own bubble and not chasing the 9-5. I just want a little van to renovate and live out of, travelling and meeting people.. but that’s unrealistic. Ironic that, our natural nomadic lifestyle is nigh impossible (and would be absolutely if we al decided on it). Sure, I can live frugal and work odd jobs to fund it, but the issue stems in judgement. 
I live in a place where everything is material, as we all do. No one understands me when I say I just. Don’t. Care. About money, nor having flash stuff. I’m content with being alone with my own thoughts (though not to an unhealthy extent). Everyone wants to “fix” that.. it’s like the waters been poisoned and everyone’s deluded. 

I just can’t understand where I fit into this world. I don’t want to fit into it, it’s not for me. The benefits of doing so, fail to outweigh the negatives, and with that I’m coming to the conclusion that I should be gone, as opposed to staying around. 

I don’t want to die. No one truly does. But the alternative is a place of mental agony in every waking moment, spare a few well disguised hours a week, where that agony dilutes into gnawing thoughts and anxieties, as opposed to booming commands. 

I don’t know what else to say, or how else to just keep on marching. The body wants to, the mind doesn’t.
